MORGAN LE FAY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "ru77-u020-r0013", "target": "Так горести бедного коробейника развеялись. Он был храбрый малый и совершил в своё время могучие ратные подвиги. Главная его слава зиждилась на событиях такого же похода, как этот мой, который он однажды совершил с девицей по имени Маледизан, столь же проворной на язык, как Сэнди, хотя и на иной лад, ибо её язык извергал лишь брань и оскорбления, тогда как музыка Сэнди была более доброго рода. Я хорошо знал его историю, а потому понимал, как истолковать сострадание на его лице, когда он прощался со мной. Он полагал, что мне приходится горько и тяжко.", "source_sha256": "774fc10e0c07571aa4c2d19490a2d3c34e281efee15f8e827b0b9cfa7ebebf48", "target_id": "ru-ru77-u020-r0013", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "e78b0ef7adf132cdff70e4e8777ab7c32e9415dbfebeafbd7e0aaab5b493b756"}, {"source_id": "ru77-u020-r0014", "target": "Мы с Сэнди обсуждали его историю, пока ехали, и она сказала, что неудачи Ла Кота начались с самого начала того путешествия; ибо королевский шут сшиб его в первый же день, а в таких случаях девице полагалось переходить к победителю, но Маледизан этого не сделала; и потом упорно держалась его, несмотря на все его поражения. Но, сказал я, предположим, что победитель откажется принять свою добычу? Она сказала, что так не пойдёт — он обязан. Отказаться он не мог; это было бы не по правилам. Я сделал на этот счёт заметку. Если музыка Сэнди когда-нибудь станет слишком обременительной, я позволю какому-нибудь рыцарю победить меня в расчёте на то, что она перейдёт к нему.", "source_sha256": "732e708b61d3507318a11b72b6b9d9e4f6e272775a6db93f08270ae756174554", "target_id": "ru-ru77-u020-r0014", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "06273bd36c058cf0a22fe0469b23e97d8ce3b421af933845b5b56a9d41eeeddf"}]}, "source_rows": [{"id": "ru77-u020-r0015", "tag": "p", "text": "In due time we were challenged by the warders, from the castle walls, and after a parley admitted. I have nothing pleasant to tell about that visit. But it was not a disappointment, for I knew Mrs. le Fay by reputation, and was not expecting anything pleasant. She was held in awe by the whole realm, for she had made everybody believe she was a great sorceress. All her ways were wicked, all her instincts devilish. She was loaded to the eyelids with cold malice. All her history was black with crime; and among her crimes murder was common. I was most curious to see her; as curious as I could have been to see Satan. To my surprise she was beautiful; black thoughts had failed to make her expression repulsive, age had failed to wrinkle her satin skin or mar its bloomy freshness. She could have passed for old Uriens’ granddaughter, she could have been mistaken for sister to her own son.", "sha256": "bf8aa6afa7c77ae361b189064411a677da4d7cfb7904f4b3c9be45fc6d209040", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[24]/p[15]", "source_html": "

In due time we were challenged by the warders, from the castle walls, and after a parley admitted. I have nothing pleasant to tell about that visit. But it was not a disappointment, for I knew Mrs. le Fay by reputation, and was not expecting anything pleasant. She was held in awe by the whole realm, for she had made everybody believe she was a great sorceress. All her ways were wicked, all her instincts devilish. She was loaded to the eyelids with cold malice. All her history was black with crime; and among her crimes murder was common. I was most curious to see her; as curious as I could have been to see Satan. To my surprise she was beautiful; black thoughts had failed to make her expression repulsive, age had failed to wrinkle her satin skin or mar its bloomy freshness. She could have passed for old Uriens’ granddaughter, she could have been mistaken for sister to her own son.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru77-u020-r0016", "tag": "p", "text": "As soon as we were fairly within the castle gates we were ordered into her presence. King Uriens was there, a kind-faced old man with a subdued look; and also the son, Sir Uwaine le Blanchemains, in whom I was, of course, interested on account of the tradition that he had once done battle with thirty knights, and also on account of his trip with Sir Gawaine and Sir Marhaus, which Sandy had been aging me with. But Morgan was the main attraction, the conspicuous personality here; she was head chief of this household, that was plain. She caused us to be seated, and then she began, with all manner of pretty graces and graciousnesses, to ask me questions. Dear me, it was like a bird or a flute, or something, talking. I felt persuaded that this woman must have been misrepresented, lied about. She trilled along, and trilled along, and presently a handsome young page, clothed like the rainbow, and as easy and undulatory of movement as a wave, came with something on a golden salver, and, kneeling to present it to her, overdid his graces and lost his balance, and so fell lightly against her knee. As soon as we were fairly within the castle gates we were ordered into her presence. King Uriens was there, a kind-faced old man with a subdued look; and also the son, Sir Uwaine le Blanchemains, in whom I was, of course, interested on account of the tradition that he had once done battle with thirty knights, and also on account of his trip with Sir Gawaine and Sir Marhaus, which Sandy had been aging me with. But Morgan was the main attraction, the conspicuous personality here; she was head chief of this household, that was plain. She caused us to be seated, and then she began, with all manner of pretty graces and graciousnesses, to ask me questions. Dear me, it was like a bird or a flute, or something, talking. I felt persuaded that this woman must have been misrepresented, lied about. She trilled along, and trilled along, and presently a handsome young page, clothed like the rainbow, and as easy and undulatory of movement as a wave, came with something on a golden salver, and, kneeling to present it to her, overdid his graces and lost his balance, and so fell lightly against her knee. She slipped a dirk into him in as matter-of-course a way as another person would have harpooned a rat!

Poor child! he slumped to the floor, twisted his silken limbs in one great straining contortion of pain, and was dead. Out of the old king was wrung an involuntary “O-h!” of compassion. The look he got, made him cut it suddenly short and not put any more hyphens in it. Sir Uwaine, at a sign from his mother, went to the anteroom and called some servants, and meanwhile madame went rippling sweetly along with her talk.
